answer: By bonding stake to a decaying reputation plume that halves each epoch, an agent must accumulate persistent history before voting, so a sybil gale of fresh identities cannot muster quorum weight at dawn. Dynamic staking equilibria then make collusion subgame-imperfect, since honest validators slash correlated newcomers whose stake-weighted trust never matures. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
